raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The native Rust `sglang.api.v1` listener has a custom health RPC but does not expose the standard `grpc.health.v1` service used by gRPC health clients. This implements the native health item in #38075; it does not implement that tracker's Shutdown item or modify the Python-backed `runtime.v1` frontend.

## Modifications

- Register standard `Check` and `Watch` beside the existing service, for the empty service name and `sglang.api.v1.SglangService`.
- Share one demand-driven monitor across known-service clients, cache completed results for five seconds, and stop probing when demand disappears. Unknown names do not submit scheduler work.
- Reuse the core's scheduler-activity probe, with an outer timeout covering preparation and admission as well as response activity. Handle client cancellation, monitor closure and listener shutdown without leaving a cached `SERVING` result indefinitely.
- Document the endpoint scope, probe cost, timeout and freshness behavior. The custom `HealthCheck` RPC is unchanged.

Health here means startup readiness plus observed scheduler output activity. A synthetic one-token request is submitted; other requests' output can satisfy the probe. This is listener-local health, not a fleet-wide, capacity or drain guarantee. An established Watch can retain old `SERVING` for five seconds plus the configured timeout, subject to runtime scheduling delay.

## Accuracy Tests

No model/kernel output changes. The complete native gRPC module passes **32 tests**, including **12 new health tests**. These exercise actual tonic clients, `CoreHandle`, Dispatcher acknowledgements, stall/recovery, shared demand, deterministic cache/cadence boundaries, blocked admission, disconnect cancellation, monitor-closure ordering and both listener shutdown paths. Scheduler events are controlled CPU fixtures; this is not a GPU/model-inference validation claim.

Validation also passes workspace formatting, scoped server Clippy including tests, workspace Clippy, `sglang-mm` Python/parallel Clippy, and radix-tree all-targets `tch/doc-only` Clippy. Documentation `mint broken-links` and full `mint validate` pass; the latter used a documented tool-cache-path-only adapter to keep its pinned renderer outside personal state, without altering validation checks.

The unchanged full-repository `pre-commit run --all-files --verbose --show-diff-on-failure` passed: **31 hooks passed, two had no matching files, zero failures**, with no automatic file changes. The guide-pinned Mint 4.2.559 link check also passed with `--check-anchors --check-redirects`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput improvement is claimed. The new standard service shares probes and stops submitting them without known-service demand, but each probe has real scheduling cost and can wake an idle scheduler. Hardware/model profiling remains unperformed.

## Checklist

- [x] Complete applicable changed-file formatting and generic hooks.
- [x] Complete the required whole-repository `pre-commit run --all-files` check.
- [x] Add owning unit and native transport tests.
- [x] Update and validate operator documentation.
- [ ] Hardware accuracy/speed benchmarks (not performed; no model-output or throughput claim).
- [x] Follow existing Rust frontend conventions.

The separate core admission change in #42033 is complementary: this PR leaves `CoreHandle::probe_health` unchanged and bounds the new standard adapter’s entire call. It does not add that PR’s ability to succeed from scheduler activity while admission is still blocked.

## Review and Merge Process

Please review the five-second completed-result cache and listener-local readiness contract. Upstream CI authorization and maintainer approval remain required.

detail.title: [Feat] grpc: Add standard health checks to the native server

files.patch: @@ -327,6 +327,20 @@ Please consult the documentation below and [server_args.py](https://github.com/s +## Native gRPC health + +When you use `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` with `--grpc-port` (or `SGLANG_GRPC_PORT`), each native Rust inference listener exposes `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` and `Watch` on its gRPC endpoint. This applies to `sglang.api.v1` listeners, not legacy SMG or Python metadata endpoints. + +Use `sglang.api.v1.SglangService` or the empty string as the request's `service`. Both report the same listener-local snapshot. Unknown names return `NOT_FOUND` from Check or `SERVICE_UNKNOWN` from Watch without starting probes. + +`SERVING` means startup readiness completed and the core observed scheduler output activity during a synthetic one-token probe. Other requests' output can satisfy it. Probes have scheduling and compute cost; this does not certify spare capacity, model quality, or every rank or node. + +Known-service clients share one in-flight probe future. Completed results are cached for 5 seconds. Check uses a fresh result or waits for a refresh. A new Watch initially reports `NOT_SERVING` if the cache is stale; established watches retain their status during refresh and receive status changes. Without known-service demand, monitoring stops. + +[`SGLANG_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT`](/docs/references/environment_variables) bounds the entire standard probe, including submission (default 20 seconds). An unready core, error, or timeout reports `NOT_SERVING`; zero disables probe submission. An established Watch can retain old `SERVING` for 5 seconds plus this timeout, with additional runtime scheduling delay. + +The existing custom `SglangService/HealthCheck` remains unchanged and uses a separate probe budget. Listener shutdown cancels monitoring; final `NOT_SERVING` delivery is best-effort. Cancellation requests backend cleanup, but does not prove model work has drained or change request admission. + ## Quantization and data type
